Local 371 Members Injured On the Job:

# Know Your Rights

**Report Every Injury Immediately**
Failure to report a work-related injury promptly is the primary reason for a worker's compensation claim to be denied. Report all work injuries immediately, and make sure a First Report of Injury is filed on time.

**Initial Medical Treatment**
Your employer will designate the doctor or facility to provide you with your initial medical treatment. You must go to the initial medical treatment facility. You must receive your first treatment at this facility. If you need further treatment, you must return to this facility. If you do not select your own physician, the doctor or facility designated by your employer will become the attending physician.

**Your Right to Choose Your Attending Physician/Provider**
After the employer provides you with your initial medical treatment, you have the right to choose your own attending physician. If you have a serious injury that is going to require extended treatment or cause you to be disabled, the Union strongly urges you to choose your own attending physician rather than continue treatment with the employer's doctor.

If your employer has a managed care plan to pay for medical care for workers' compensation cases you must go to their panel of doctors to select your attending physician but he or she must not be but for the doctor's purpose. If your employer has a mistake to make one of the doctors who is on the panel. The union can assist you in this.

If your employer does not have a managed care plan, the union will assist you. You can select any physician named as your attending physician any physician named by the state Compensation Commission.

Once you have established an attending physician, you cannot change doctors unless: (1) the attending physician refers you to another doctor; (2) the insurance company grants permission for you to change doctors; or (3) the Workers' Compensation Commission authorizes you to use another doctor.

**Examination Requirements**
Even if you have your own attending physician, the insurance company or your employer can require you to submit for examination by another physician. This doctor can only suggest treatment from another doctor against your own doctor's advice.

**Billing for Medical Treatment**
- Bills for your medical treatment should be sent by the medical provider directly to your employer's worker's compensation insurance carrier to be paid. Make sure you know who that insurance carrier is and tell the doctor's office. If you have paid out-of-pocket expenses for prescriptions, these must be reimbursed in full by the worker's compensation insurance carrier.

**Medical Treatment/Therapy**
If you can continue to work but you need medical treatment or therapy, this should be done during your work hour if available with this loss of pay. If it is not available during work hours, you must go on your own time, too. If you have stated medical expenses for your treatment, you should be reimbursed for your travel expenses at the rate of 15¢ per mile. The insurance company pays.
